headline: MAY PCE DROPS TODAY: GOLD TESTING $4,000 FLOOR AS INFLATION DATA SETS FED HIKE ODDS
snippet: May PCE — the Fed's preferred inflation gauge — releases Thursday at 8:30 AM ET alongside Q1 GDP, jobless claims, and durable goods, with consensus expecting headline PCE at 4.1% YoY; GoldSilver.com warns that if the print arrives at or above the FOMC's revised year-end PCE forecast of 3.6%, the nine hawkish dots in the June projections become a floor not a ceiling, potentially locking in September hike odds at the current 70% CME FedWatch level and extending gold's correction below $4,000. The real question is whether Iran-driven oil disinflation building in June shows up early in May data — a cooler-than-expected print could snap the Swiss-franc-takes-the-haven-crown narrative and restore gold's bid, with spot having bounced to ~$4,134 this morning from Wednesday's $3,970 low.

headline: ING CUTS GOLD TO $4,300 Q3 — BUT CHINA POSTS BIGGEST IMPORT MONTH IN 2 YEARS AND ETFs SNAP OUTFLOW STREAK
snippet: GoldSilver.com's June 24 counter-narrative analysis finds the selloff's surface signal at odds with the underlying data: ING cut its Q3 gold forecast from $4,850 to $4,300 (Q4: $4,600) following the hawkish FOMC, yet China's gold imports hit their biggest single month in two years in May, gold ETFs snapped a four-week outflow streak, and every major bank's year-end target — Goldman $4,900, ING $4,600, JPMorgan $6,000 — sits 15–50% above spot. The article frames ING's move as a tactical rate-model adjustment while noting the structural bullish case (central bank tonnage demand, ETF re-accumulation, chronic physical deficit in silver) remains intact — and that any PCE print below consensus on Thursday mechanically reverses the Fed-hike-premium that drove both the dollar rally and the gold flush.

headline: NINE MILE METALS FINDS TWO MASSIVE SULPHIDE ZONES IN 129.72m VMS CORRIDOR — BATHURST CAMP (CSE:NINE)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Nine Mile Metals Ltd. (CSE:NINE)
snippet: Nine Mile Metals Ltd. (CSE:NINE) announced June 24 the completion of DDH WD-26-01 at its Wedge Mine property in the Bathurst Mining Camp, New Brunswick, intersecting 129.72 metres of continuous visual Cu-Zn-Pb-Ag sulphide mineralization from 34.6 to 164.3 metres downhole — including two distinct massive sulphide horizons, with the lower zone accompanied by visible sphalerite (Zn) and galena (Pb) confirming the classic VMS deposit architecture expected in the world-class Bathurst Camp. Lab-certified assays are pending, but the unbroken visual mineralization across 129.72 metres of a 202-metre hole — and the structural confirmation of two separate massive sulphide zones — builds on WD-26-02's recent 234.15-metre visual mineralization and new copper-rich VMS horizon at the same target, suggesting Nine Mile's Wedge Mine targeting model is systematically tracking the deposit footprint.

headline: WESDOME CONFIRMS NEW 150m PARALLEL ZONE AT KIENA DEEP — 42.1m AT 6.9 g/t AU, OPEN IN ALL DIRECTIONS (TSX:WDO)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Wesdome Gold Mines (TSX:WDO)
snippet: Wesdome Gold Mines Ltd. (TSX:WDO) announced June 22 the discovery of an entirely new mineralized corridor at Kiena in Val-d'Or, Québec: drill hole N134-7152W1 in the previously untested Norbenite Footwall area returned 42.1 metres at 6.9 g/t gold uncapped, confirming an at-least-150-vertical-metre high-grade zone that remains open in all directions and is accessible from existing underground development. Wesdome simultaneously extended high-grade mineralization across multiple Eagle River zones at depth and plans a Q3 2026 technical review with preliminary metallurgical testing for the new zone — findings that collectively demonstrate Kiena Deep's orebody footprint substantially exceeds current mine plans.

headline: COPPER GIANT CONFIRMS 3rd CORRIDOR AT MOCOA — 1,052m CONTINUOUS MINERALIZATION BELOW PIT (TSXV:CGNT)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Copper Giant Resources (TSXV:CGNT)
snippet: Copper Giant Resources Corp. (TSXV:CGNT) released June 22 assays from deep infill drilling at the Mocoa copper-molybdenum porphyry in Colombia: drill hole MD-064 intersected 1,052 metres of continuous mineralization including 486 metres at 0.57% CuEq and a 180-metre interval at 0.44% CuEq (0.36% Cu, 0.015% Mo) — grades exceeding the current MRE average of 0.51% CuEq — while companion hole MD-063 confirmed the western breccia as a third distinct drill-tested mineralized corridor and extended continuous mineralization below the current conceptual pit into ground previously modelled as waste. With a third drill rig simultaneously testing the La Estrella target from the opposite end of the same corridor, Mocoa's multi-phase porphyry system is tracking toward resource upside well beyond the current estimate.

headline: MACKAY GOLD ACQUIRES COMSTOCK NEVADA ASSETS FOR $45M — LARGEST CLAIM BLOCK IN 167-YEAR DISTRICT HISTORY (TSXV:MACK)
snippet: Mackay Gold & Silver Corp. (TSXV:MACK) announced June 22 a Securities Purchase Agreement to acquire 100% of Comstock Inc.'s Nevada mining assets — all patented and unpatented mining claims, processing facilities, permits, and water rights in Storey and Lyon Counties — for over $45 million in aggregate consideration (>$30M cash and stock, a retained 1.5% NSR royalty, assumption of all reclamation liabilities, and a $10M contingent payment), expanding Mackay's land position 70% to 4,343 hectares and creating the largest consolidated claim package in the Comstock District's 167-year history. For Comstock Inc., the divestiture funds its strategic pivot from junior mining into renewable metals and materials applications, reducing its annual costs by more than $1.5 million.

headline: ASTON BAY STORM COPPER PFS DUE Q3 — NUNAVUT GOVERNMENT BACKS PROJECT, NIRB SUBMISSION IN FINAL REVIEW (TSXV:BAY)
source_name: Globe and Mail / Aston Bay Holdings (TSXV:BAY)
snippet: Aston Bay Holdings Ltd. (TSXV:BAY) provided a June 24 development update confirming that the Pre-Feasibility Study for its Storm Copper Project on Somerset Island, Nunavut — operated under an 80/20 JV by American West Metals — is on track for Q3 2026 completion with Sacre Davey, Ausenco, and the Nuna Group conducting process plant and flowsheet optimization, while the Nunavut Planning Commission is in final review of the mine permit application and the Nunavut Government committed up to CA$100,000 toward community liaison activities. Storm Copper targets 2028 regulatory approvals, placing it among the first Arctic copper projects to advance toward construction at a time when Section 232 tariff policy is creating strong structural incentives for North American domestic copper supply development.

headline: GOLDMAN CUTS GOLD TO $4,900; JPMORGAN HOLDS $6,000 — THE $1,400 GAP EXPOSES TWO IRRECONCILABLE FRAMEWORKS
snippet: When Goldman Sachs cut its 2026 year-end gold target from $5,400 to $4,900 on June 19 — citing the Fed's delay of rate cuts to June 2027 as eliminating the rate-channel tailwind — JPMorgan kept its $6,000 target and Wells Fargo held $6,100–$6,300, because their models treat gold as a reserve asset driven by committed central-bank, ETF, and physical tonnage demand that is largely insensitive to short-term rate changes. GoldSilver.com's analysis of the $1,400 spread argues the divergence matters for junior mining investors because whichever framework proves correct determines whether gold's correction has another leg down (Goldman's rate-model view) or has already hit structural support (JPMorgan's reserve-demand view) — and the real-world data point to watch is central bank purchase tonnage, which has stayed above 1,000 tonnes annually for three straight years regardless of rates.

headline: SIXTH STRAIGHT DEFICIT AND 67:1 RATIO SAY SILVER'S CORRECTION IS THE SETUP, NOT THE REVERSAL
snippet: GoldSilver.com's June 2026 silver outlook argues that silver's 42% collapse from January's $121.62 all-time high is the classic contrarian setup: the global market is tracking toward a sixth consecutive annual supply deficit of 46.3 million ounces (wider than the prior year), the gold-silver ratio at 67:1 is at its widest since the Iran war's peak, and year-over-year silver price remains up more than 161%. The bullish year-end target of $90–$106 depends on oil disinflation enabling the Fed to pause its hawkish trajectory; the bear case ($60–$63 retest) requires the Iran ceasefire to break down and oil to re-spike above $100 — and the article notes that the same thesis that drove silver from $30 to $121 in 2024–2025 (structural industrial deficit plus monetary haven demand) remains structurally intact even as the rate premium temporarily overwhelms it.

headline: MORGAN STANLEY: GOLD NEEDS MEANINGFUL ETF INFLOW REBOUND TO UNLOCK $5,200 TARGET
snippet: Morgan Stanley commodity strategists published June 22 a note arguing that gold will struggle to reach the bank's own $5,200 year-end target without a meaningful rebound in ETF inflows in the second half — noting that 2025's record $89 billion in ETF inflows was the primary fuel for gold's rally from $1,800 to $5,589, and that the four-week outflow streak that preceded the current correction needs to reverse before the market can re-rate to the H2 objective. The note identifies three variables: Fed hawkishness (negative for rate-sensitive ETF demand), ETF flow direction (the structural swing factor), and Middle East geopolitical risk (now reduced by the Iran ceasefire) — and was followed within days by gold ETFs snapping their four-week outflow streak, a single-week data point that may signal the inflection Morgan Stanley identified as the key unlock condition for the bull case.
